message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 40 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 (filled at $222.90, ~$8,916 total).

**Summary:** I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended September 28, 2024, filed November 1, 2024) and found a business that is growing modestly but with improving quality of earnings: total net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, driven by Services up 13% to $96.2 billion (73.9% gross margin) while iPhone was roughly flat at $201.2 billion and Greater China declined 8%; total gross margin expanded to 46.2% from 44.1%, lifting operating income to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion. Net income fell to $93.7 billion (diluted EPS $6.08) versus $97.0 billion the prior year, but that decline was entirely due to a one-time $10.2 billion net tax charge from the European Commission's State Aid Decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%) — operating performance actually improved. Cash generation remains exceptional at $118.3 billion of operating cash flow, and the balance sheet carries $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities against $97.3 billion of term debt, with $95.0 billion returned via buybacks and $15.2 billion in dividends. Risks I weighed include the DOJ antitrust suit, EU DMA noncompliance proceedings (fines of up to 10% of worldwide net sales), and Greater China weakness, but at ~36.6x trailing EPS the valuation is reasonable for a franchise with this cash flow and capital-return profile. I therefore bought 40 shares at a limit of $222.90, essentially the current market (last $222.70, ask $222.72), for about $8,916 — within the $10,000 per-order cap and the $20,000 daily cap, using existing cash with no money moved out of the account.
